title: RatHat Android Malware Uses AI and ADB to Steal Banking Credentials and OTPs
content_md: The malware uses artificial intelligence, Accessibility Service abuse, and Android Debug Bridge (ADB) pairing to steal banking credentials, payment PINs, one-time passwords, and lock-screen data. RatHat is spread through smishing messages, malicious advertisements, phishing websites, and third-party download portals. Victims are lured into manually installing APK files disguised as legitimate apps, including streaming services, browsers, and financial applications. Unlike common Android malware, RatHat does not rely only on its malicious app. It uses a multi-stage infection chain to gain shell-level access, deploy native tools, and remain active even after the victim removes the original application. RatHat Steals Banking OTPs After installation, RatHat attempts to convince victims to enable its Accessibility Service. It uses localized HTML pages and financial or network-related lures to obtain the permission. Once granted, the malware automates several sensitive actions. It opens Developer Options, taps the Build Number setting seven times, enables Wireless Debugging, and reads the ADB pairing code and port number displayed on the device screen. Phishing site distributing RatHat malware (Source: zimperium) RatHat then uses its embedded ADB library to pair with the device’s local ADB daemon.
